title: psychological prison time
content:
a few weeks ago, there was a day when I felt like this — like I was sitting alone in a dark prison cell, staring at black walls and a single window, wondering what I did wrong to be here, in this dark solitary confinement. why do I feel like I am being punished? in that prison place, time no longer seemed to exist. there was a single bird fluttering, attempting to escape. mostly I just sat there in silence, in wearing a cloak the color of blood.

~

I’ve been wanting to challenge myself to do one animated drawing a day — each lasting a second, so that, after a month, I’ll have a 30 second animation of how I lived and metabolized that month.

some years ago, I made mood diaries. this reminds me of that. sometimes I am terrified and overwhelmed by the intensity of my own internal experiences, but I do find that writing and drawing them helps. it creates a container to hold them, so that I feel a little less alone. it helps me find distance from my experiences; the kind of distance which allows me to breathe and know that this, too, will pass.
